claims.text: At stage-2, ProductsController.List() takes [FromQuery] int limit = 20 with Range(1, MaxPageSize) where MaxPageSize = 100, and [FromQuery] int offset = 0 with Range(0, int.MaxValue).
List() builds db.Products.OrderBy(p => p.Id).Skip(offset).Take(limit).Select(ProductDto) and runs it with ToListAsync(), returning Ok(page).

EF Core with the Npgsql provider translates OrderBy/Skip/Take into ORDER BY ... LIMIT ... OFFSET ...; for a request without maxPriceVnd the stage-2 api logs SQL ending 'ORDER BY p.id LIMIT @p1 OFFSET @p', limit and offset sent as parameter values.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Complex query operators / pagination; api log category Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command (lab, stage-2)

claims.text: Without ORDER BY, SQL does not define row order; PostgreSQL may return rows in any order and it can differ between executions, so LIMIT/OFFSET without an ORDER BY giving a unique order can yield inconsistent (overlapping or missing) pages.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: 7.6 LIMIT and OFFSET; 7.5 Sorting Rows

claims.text: ASP.NET Core validates attributes like Range on action parameters; [ApiController] makes a failure answer 400 automatically, before the action runs, with a ValidationProblemDetails body whose errors entry names the parameter.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Create web APIs, ApiController attribute, Automatic HTTP 400 responses

claims.text: [FromQuery] binds a parameter from the query string; a parameter left out of the request keeps its C# default value (limit 20, offset 0).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Model binding, Sources / [FromQuery]; optional parameters with default values

claims.text: The endpoint refuses a limit outside 1..100 with 400 instead of clamping it to 100.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang ProductsController.cs stage-2 lines 17-27; DECISIONS.md §3 /repo-stage 2 A1

claims.text: Running lab at stage-2: GET /api/v1/products?limit=3&offset=2 returns products with id 3, 4, 5; GET ?limit=101 returns 400 application/problem+json with errors.limit 'The field limit must be between 1 and 100.'
claims.source_hint: lab at stage-2: curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products?limit=3&offset=2 and ?limit=101; db seed (8 products)

claims.text: In an unquoted shell command, & ends the command and runs it in the background, so a URL containing & must be quoted.
claims.source_hint: Bash reference manual: Lists of Commands (the & control operator)

claims.text: A query parameter is a name=value pair after '?' in a URL (pairs joined by '&' by convention) that the server reads as an option; [FromQuery] binds it by name. Here the path still points at the product collection.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Model binding, query string source; RFC 9110 section 4.2 (http URI, query component)

claims.text: Without pagination the whole cost (reading every row, serializing every row to JSON, sending it) is paid before the client can hide rows, so hiding rows in the app saves none of it.
claims.source_hint: general reasoning from the request flow shown in section 4

claims.text: Refusing an over-large limit with 400 (rather than silently shrinking it) is preferable when you want the client to learn its request was wrong; clamping is the alternative some APIs choose.
claims.source_hint: API design convention; Đơn Hàng chose to refuse

claims.text: OFFSET counts row positions at query time; a row inserted or deleted before the page position between two requests shifts later rows, so offset pages can repeat or skip a row even with ORDER BY on a unique column.
